newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Bersani sees limited mini-budget for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bersani sees limited mini-budget for 1997.

text.p: Italy's Minister of Labour Pierluigi Bersani on Wednesday said that a planned mini-budget for 1997 would be limited as the Italian economy's progress early this year was steady.
Bersani told reporters in parliament that Italy had progressed in the first few months of 1997, and the government now had the opportunity to introduce a mini-budget of limited proportions.
Earlier, Prime Minister Romano Prodi confirmed that Italy will introduce a mini-budget in the next few weeks.

Bersani confirmed that the GDP growth of two percent in 1997 forecast last autumn would be difficult to achieve. Government sources have recently said that Italian GDP will grow at a rate of 1.0-1.5 percent this year.
Meanwhile, the leader of one of Italy's leading union CISL Sergio D'Antoni warned the government over cutting social spending in the planned mini-budget.
"For us, it is a problem of content. If it (the mini-budget) cuts social spending we will be against it," he said in a interview on Italian television.
